scenario_name: Trace data-architecture decisions to assessment criteria
scenario_description: Update the DE0745 constructive-alignment goal so assessed data-architecture decisions are explicitly linked to outcomes, artefacts and downstream reuse.
trigger_evidence: Review of the baseline model found that assessment percentages were explicit, but the architectural decisions evidenced by each task were not traceable.
before_json: {"description": "Ensure every intended course capability is developed through suitable activity and directly assessed using the official assessment architecture: Practical work 60%; semester tests 20%; exam 20%."}
after_json: {"description": "Every assessed data-architecture decision must be linked to a stated course outcome, a named evidence artefact and the downstream enterprise-case activity that may reuse it."}
driver: Strengthen constructive alignment without changing the approved DE0745 workload or assessment weighting.

scenario_name: Require task-level outcome and evidence traceability
scenario_description: Update the DE0745 traceability rule so every summative task identifies the outcome, architectural decision and reusable evidence artefact it assesses.
trigger_evidence: Current mappings identify broad outcome coverage but do not identify the specific evidence produced by each task.
before_json: {"description": "Every curriculum outcome in DE0745 course curriculum must be connected to responsible curriculum components and direct assessment evidence before the model is approved."}
after_json: {"description": "Each summative task must identify the outcome assessed, the data-architecture decision evidenced, the rubric criterion used and any downstream curriculum artefact that may reuse the evidence."}
driver: Make assessment traceability sufficiently precise for cross-course curriculum review.

scenario_name: Define the systems-theory prerequisite competence profile
scenario_description: Replace the unspecified DE0752 prerequisite profile with an explicit set of systems reasoning competencies expected by downstream courses.
trigger_evidence: The baseline states that there is no formal prerequisite, but programme review found that later courses assume modelling and systems-analysis competencies.
after_json: {"description": "Expected prerequisite competence includes systems thinking, causal modelling, feedback analysis and the ability to interpret formal and conceptual models; gaps must be diagnosed before dependent course work."}
driver: Make hidden prerequisite assumptions visible without introducing a new formal admission prerequisite.

scenario_name: Map enterprise-case evidence across course boundaries
scenario_description: Update the DE0751 mapping process to record incoming artefacts from earlier courses and the programme outcomes evidenced by the final e-business project.
trigger_evidence: The baseline process maps local outcomes and assessments but does not record the lineage of evidence reused from sibling courses.
before_json: {"description": "Map outcomes to curriculum components, learning activities, assessments and evidence; identify missing, weak or excessive coverage."}
after_json: {"description": "Map DE0751 outcomes, activities and assessments to incoming data, architecture and process artefacts, record their provenance and identify the programme outcomes evidenced by the integrated project."}
driver: Create a complete longitudinal evidence map for the culminating e-business assessment.

scenario_name: Make the programme director accountable for cross-course impact closure
scenario_description: Extend the Business Informatics programme-director role with explicit accountability for resolving cross-course impact notifications.
trigger_evidence: The baseline role owns the local programme model but does not explicitly require closure of unresolved sibling-course impacts.
before_json: {"description": "Role accountable for maintaining the local curriculum model, evidence and justified changes for Business Informatics programme."}
after_json: {"description": "The programme director maintains the programme model, assigns owners for cross-course impacts, verifies that notified courses respond and records the final programme-level decision and rationale."}
driver: Create clear accountability for completing cross-course curriculum-change reviews.

scenario_name: Identify prerequisite and hand-off impacts automatically
scenario_description: Extend the DE0747 impact-analysis requirement so the system identifies courses affected by changed prerequisites, shared concepts or enterprise-case artefacts.
trigger_evidence: The baseline functional requirement identifies affected units generally but does not specify dependency categories needed for curriculum propagation.
before_json: {"description": "Given a proposed change, identify affected parent, child and sibling curriculum units through outcome, prerequisite, assessment, workload and shared-concept links."}
after_json: {"description": "Given a changed prerequisite, shared concept, outcome mapping, assessment artefact or sequence dependency, identify every affected parent and sibling unit and return the dependency path and evidence used."}
driver: Make prerequisite and cross-course impact identification reproducible rather than dependent on manual recall.

scenario_name: Validate mathematical prerequisites before expanding ML scope
scenario_description: Update the DE0937 workload goal so new algorithms may be added only after prerequisite diagnostics and explicit workload trade-offs.
trigger_evidence: The baseline lists mathematics, probability and statistics prerequisites, but does not require evidence that students possess them before advanced algorithm coverage expands.
before_json: {"description": "Maintain 64 contact and 96 independent-work hours (160 total) and validate the prerequisite basis: Mathematics, probability theory and mathematical statistics."}
after_json: {"description": "Preserve the approved 6 ECTS workload and add new algorithm families only when prerequisite diagnostics confirm mathematics, probability and statistics readiness and an equivalent content trade-off is recorded."}
driver: Protect prerequisite integrity and prevent tool-driven scope growth in Machine Learning Algorithms.

scenario_name: Require explicit trade-offs for language and tool additions
scenario_description: Update the DE0759 workload-conservation rule so every new language, framework or toolchain replaces equivalent assessed content.
trigger_evidence: The baseline preserves credits and hours but does not require a named removal when new technology-specific content is added.
before_json: {"description": "Curriculum changes in DE0759 course curriculum must preserve approved credit volume and must explicitly reallocate learning and assessment workload when scope is added or removed."}
after_json: {"description": "Adding a programming language, framework or toolchain requires a documented removal or reduction of equivalent learning and assessment workload while preserving conceptual comparison outcomes."}
driver: Prevent language-specific scope growth from displacing stable object-oriented concepts.

scenario_name: Define the AI curriculum scope profile
scenario_description: Refine the DE0478 scope concept to distinguish foundational AI reasoning from machine-learning algorithm depth and tool-specific implementation.
trigger_evidence: Programme review found overlap between Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Algorithms without a modelled boundary.
before_json: {"description": "Intelligent agents, search, knowledge representation, inference, planning, uncertainty, decision making and learning agents."}
after_json: {"description": "The DE0478 scope profile identifies foundational search, knowledge representation, reasoning and intelligent-system integration, while advanced statistical learning algorithms and comparative model evaluation are assigned to DE0937."}
driver: Clarify assessment responsibility and reduce duplication between AI and machine learning.

scenario_name: Engineer a coherent software and AI progression map
scenario_description: Update the Computer Systems portfolio process to model the progression from requirements through implementation and testing into AI and machine-learning applications.
trigger_evidence: The baseline process sequences courses generally but does not identify the common artefacts and evidence chain joining the software and AI pathways.
before_json: {"description": "Allocate outcome responsibility, sequence courses, test prerequisite feasibility and protect the thesis pathway."}
after_json: {"description": "Allocate outcome responsibility, sequence requirements, implementation, testing, AI and machine-learning courses, identify common artefacts and verify prerequisite feasibility and thesis-path continuity."}
driver: Create an explicit progression map across software-engineering and intelligent-systems courses.

scenario_name: Add statistical validity and ethics expertise to ML review
scenario_description: Refine the DE0937 course-review-panel role so curriculum changes are reviewed for statistical validity, reproducibility and responsible use.
trigger_evidence: The baseline panel checks evidence and cross-unit effects but does not name expertise needed for machine-learning assessment quality.
before_json: {"description": "Collective review role responsible for challenging evidence, checking cross-unit effects and deciding whether curriculum changes are acceptable."}
after_json: {"description": "The course-review panel must include or consult expertise in statistical validity, reproducibility, data governance and responsible AI when reviewing machine-learning outcomes and assessments."}
driver: Ensure ML assessment coverage is credible and responsibly governed.

scenario_description: Strengthen the DE0759 auditability requirement so every curriculum artefact records the language, toolchain and environment used.
trigger_evidence: The baseline preserves model-change provenance but does not capture technology versions needed to reproduce object-oriented implementation evidence.
before_json: {"description": "Every element and relationship must retain its owning fractal unit, last change, change type and driver so that decisions can be reconstructed."}
after_json: {"description": "Every element, relationship and assessment artefact must retain its owning unit, change driver, language and toolchain versions, execution environment, effective curriculum version and approval history."}
driver: Make technology-specific curriculum evidence reproducible and auditable.
